name: Mistral
profile:
## Mistral AI — Hackathon Builder Profile

### Capabilities and APIs you can use in a weekend
- **Core model API** via **Studio / Inference**: send prompts, compare models in the playground, and make first API requests with SDKs.
- **Structured outputs**: extract validated objects from text with schemas.
- **Tool/function calling**: let models call your Python functions.
- **Multimodal**: analyze images; use **Mistral Large 4** and other multimodal models.
- **Embeddings**: build semantic search or retrieval features.
- **Audio**: speech-to-text, real-time transcription, text-to-speech, and **voice agents**.
- **RAG / search**: libraries, search indices, Search Toolkit, and grounded Q&A.
- **Agents / workflows**: build agents, add context, evaluate, deploy, and observe them; create durable workflows.
- **Prompts and Skills**: store reusable prompts, package repeatable methods, and version them.
- **Connectors**: register external tools and hand them to agents.
- **Safety / moderation**: classify inputs and block unsafe content with guardrails.
- **Observability**: traces, evaluations, and online evaluations.
- **Batch jobs**: run many requests from a file.

### Hero use cases the docs emphasize
- **Productivity and coding agents** (Vibe Work / Vibe Code).
- **Voice experiences**: transcription, speech generation, and voice agents.
- **Document and knowledge apps**: RAG over libraries, search indices, and grounded answers.
- **Agentic apps and workflows**: end-to-end agents with context, tools, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
- **Data analysis**: upload spreadsheets and ask questions in plain language.
- **Full-stack app scaffolding**: describe an app in natural language and generate the structure/files.

### What it rewards in hackathon projects
The docs don’t mention hackathon judge criteria or prizes. But they clearly encourage projects that show:
- **End-to-end shipping**: build, deploy, and observe an app/agent.
- **Reusable structure**: prompts, skills, workflows, and connectors.
- **Multimodal or voice interaction**
- **Grounded / retrieval-based answers**
- **Evaluation and observability**
- **Safe inputs and moderation**

### Recent or notable features worth building on now
- **Mistral Large 4**: state-of-the-art open-weight, general-purpose multimodal model.
- **Mistral Small 4**: hybrid model combining instruct, reasoning, and coding.
- **Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3**: strong transcription and diarization.
- **OCR 4.1**: paragraph-level bounding boxes, structural block labels, and block-level confidence scores.
- **1M-token context third-party models** listed in the docs, including **Z.ai GLM 5.3** and **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017**.
- **Search Toolkit**, **online evaluations**, and **managed workflow deployment** for production-style hackathon demos.

prior_art.excerpt: ## Inspiration Devin automates part of the software engineering work. We automate the work of sales teams. There's been great progress in animating faces but nothing is interactive. That's where we come in. ## What it does We create a sales person that has a human face and a Mistral brain. It will answer any questions your client might have based on your website content. # How we built it We built this by combining various technologies and APIs to achieve the goal of allowing users to communicate with an AI avatar about a website, powered by Mistral. Our tech stack includes Mistral, OpenAI Whisper, OpenVoice, Heygen, Beautiful Soup, and Framer.
